summary: Virginia Forest Service 100-ft steel tower reported complete near Ninde in July 1950; the lookout list marks it gone; no source describes the site now.

facts.status_note: The lookout list marks it gone; no source describes what remains at the site

events.note: July 1950 item: recently completed at Ninde; the 110th tower the Forest Service erected

evidence.supports: tower recently completed at Ninde in July 1950; to be used to enforce the 4 o'clock burning law and for fire spotting
evidence.quote: The firetower recently completed at Ninde in King George County will be used in enforcing the 4 o'clock burning law as well as for regular fire spotting, according to Lloyd Farmer, chief forest warden.

evidence.supports: 100-foot steel tower; the 110th the Virginia Forest Service erected
evidence.quote: The 100-foot steel tower is the 110th erected by the Virginia Forest Service, Farmer said.

evidence.supports: lookout list entry King George (Circle): coordinates 38.26899, -77.13837; status Gone
Ninde community coordinates 38 16 16 N, 77 3 18 W, several km east of the list coordinates

sources.title: King George (Circle), Forest Lookouts (quoting The Free Lance-Star, July 8, 1950)
Virginia, Forest Fire Lookout Association lookout list

notes_for_editor: Location is unresolved: the 1950 item says Ninde, while the list coordinates (38.26899, -77.13837) sit several km west of Ninde's Wikipedia point (38.27111, -77.055). The 'Circle' name is not explained by any source read. Gone status comes only from the FFLA list; the Forest Lookouts page has no status line. Agency and height in the brief match the sources. No access, staffing or fire sources found; no new photos found; a King George County survey document about Ninde returned no text when read.
